page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-192 is a compute-focused virtual machine designed for scalable, multi-threaded processing requiring high core density. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server is powered by AMD EPYC 9B45 processors configured with 96 physical cores and two threads per core, providing 192 dedicated vCPUs. It is equipped with 360 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.88 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, backed by instruction set extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support, as well as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration.

Across benchmark evaluations, the c4d-highcpu-192 consistently scores within the top tier. It achieves top-decile results in multi-core compute metrics, including a stress-ng score of 328,676.05 and Geekbench multi-core score of 29,479. Memory bandwidth is similarly capable, registering 517.96 GB/sec in uncached read operations and 225.40 GB/sec in write operations. The system records strong results in software compilation, ray tracing, and high-throughput static web serving. In inference evaluations, prompt processing for small and medium language models ranks in the top 10%, though text generation speed for small models falls into the average tier. The server bundles no local NVMe storage and includes zero GPUs, necessitating external network-attached storage for stateful workloads.

By maximizing core count relative to RAM, the c4d-highcpu-192 provides favorable cost efficiency for pure compute workloads that do not demand extensive per-core memory footprints. The 1.88 GB per vCPU ratio represents a direct tradeoff, making this machine unsuitable for large in-memory database arrays. It is best suited for parallel batch processing, Clang and software build farms, CI/CD runners, distributed media encoding, and high-throughput stateless application serving.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highcpu-192 is a high-density, compute-optimized virtual machine engineered for compute-heavy parallel tasks. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor delivering 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores alongside 360 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.88 GB per vCPU allocation. The hardware platform includes AVX-512 vector extensions (encompassing VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic acceleration. It does not bundle local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators, meaning workloads rely on external networked storage for persistence. Benchmark results place this instance in the top decile for multi-threaded compute, memory bandwidth, Clang software compilation, and Redis operations. While prompt processing and batch processing excel, text generation benchmarks for small language models show average performance. The instance provides strong compute cost efficiency for CPU-bound infrastructure, making it well suited for extensive CI/CD pipelines, video encoding, static web rendering, and distributed computational jobs.
